label: early original-phase step: first occurrence of l/z/1/a/q/n/s/k/p/b in a sequence that begins with e/3/t/u/o
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, never at the delimiter or during copying, and never at t=0 or t=1. It peaks at t=3-4 (68% of mass) and fades by t=8. The current input token matters most: l has the highest rate (7.5x lift, 28% of mass), then z and 1, then a/q/n/s/k/p/b. Tokens like w and f almost never trigger it. Activation is mostly on the first occurrence of the token (95% of mass). It is gated by sequence context: much more likely when the sequence begins with e, 3, t, u or o (first_tok e has 5.3x lift) and when tokens two steps back are 3/e/t/o. The top examples are all l at t=4-5 after a prefix made of e/3/t/u/o tokens. This reads as a conjunction of the current token identity and an accumulated-prefix signal; the predicate approximates it with only modest precision. Many steps with a qualifying token and prefix stay below threshold, so the real context dependence is graded and spread over several prefix tokens.
